answer: Because the willow index resolves every citation against the vault checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the plume audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 35 aliases thus pays the authoring cost 35 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 39 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
